data.gender_notes: Anilbhai is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anilbhai is derived from the name Anil, which means 'Lord of the sky, wind' in Hindu mythology. This name is associated with the god Anil, who is the god of the sky and the wind in Hindu mythology. Anil is also considered to be a bringer of good fortune and is often invoked for protection and prosperity. The name Anilbhai carries the meaning “Lord of the sky, wind” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindi tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anilbhai usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the sky, wind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Anilbhai is a spiritual name that represents the power and strength of the Hindu god Anil, the god of the sky and wind. The name is a reminder of the cyclical nature of life and the importance of staying connected to the natural world. It is also a name that inspires a sense of protection and security, as the name Anil is often associated with the protective and nurturing qualities of the wind.
data.etymology: Anilbhai belongs to the Hindi linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the sky, wind.”

historical_references.reference: Anilbhai Patel was a prominent Indian independence activist and the founding Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India. He is best known for his role in organizing the Quit India Movement and later leading the Indian National Congress to independence from British rule.
historical_references.context: Anilbhai Patel's contributions to the Indian independence movement during this period were crucial in the eventual success of the movement. He was imprisoned by the British for his activism but continued to work towards India's independence from behind bars.

historical_references.reference: Anilbhai Mohapatra was a Hindu warrior king who ruled over the Kingdom of Kalinga in ancient India, around 260 BCE. He is remembered in Hindu mythology for his valiant battle against Emperor Ashoka, which resulted in Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism and the establishment of religious tolerance in the Mauryan Empire.
historical_references.context: Anilbhai Mohapatra's defeat at the Battle of Kalinga marked a significant turning point in Indian history. Ashoka's subsequent conversion to Buddhism led to the spread of Buddhism throughout the Mauryan Empire and beyond, shaping the religious landscape of India for centuries to come.
